result:
On load, the app asks the server who is signed in before it renders anything. `AppProvider` in `src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the whole tree in `AuthLoader`, which `src/lib/auth.tsx` creates with `configureAuth` from `react-query-auth`. Its `userFn` is `getUser`, which calls `GET /auth/me` through the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. That instance sends credentials, so the session cookie goes with the request. While the call is pending, `AuthLoader` shows a spinner. Components then read the result through `useUser()`, which gives `user.data` (the user) or nothing. `ProtectedRoute` in `src/lib/auth.tsx` wraps the `/app` routes in `src/app/router.tsx`. If there is no user, it redirects to `/auth/login?redirectTo=<current path>`. `AuthLayout` in `src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx` does the reverse on the login and register pages: if a user is already signed in, it navigates to `redirectTo` or the dashboard.

When any API request returns 401, the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` runs. It first adds an error toast with the server's message (or the Axios message). If the status is 401, it sets `window.location.href` to the login path from `src/config/paths.ts`, with `redirectTo` set to the current pathname. That is a full-page navigation, so the in-memory state is discarded.

The code has two problems with this. First, the 401 branch builds `new URLSearchParams()` empty and then reads `redirectTo` from it, so the lookup always returns null. The redirect target is therefore always `window.location.pathname`, which drops the query string and hash, and the `redirectTo` already in the URL is ignored. Second, the interceptor also applies to the `/auth/me` call that runs on every load. An anonymous visitor who opens `/` gets a 401 from `/auth/me`, sees an error toast, and is redirected to login with `redirectTo=/`. The landing page's "Get started" flow is therefore probably not reached as intended. I read this from the code and did not run the app to confirm it.
